voyage.name: Simon Fraser Red Leafs
voyage.content: Represent Simon Fraser University in Burnaby. The Red Leafs sponsor teams in seven men's sports and nine women's sports. Notably, SFU is the only Canadian school that's a member of the U.S. NCAA, though they are in Division II, competing with mostly smaller, regional U.S. institutions. SFU no longer plays football, either American or Canadian; it had played under American rules in the NCAA, but logistical complicatio

voyage.name: UBC Thunderbirds
voyage.content: Represent the University of British Columbia in the University Endowment Lands at the west edge of the Point Grey peninsula. The Thunderbirds field teams in 15 men's sports and 14 women's sports. Unlike SFU, UBC is a member of Canada's governing body for university sport, U Sports.

voyage.name: Robson Street
voyage.content: In the City Centre is home to many touristy shops. The neighbouring Alberni intersection is also home to a variety of high-end shops such as Louis Vuitton and Hermès.

voyage.name: Pacific Centre
voyage.content: Located in the City Centre. Has more than 150 shops, restaurants and services if you want to walk in an underground shopping centre. The shopping centre begins at its north end at Robson Street, and stretches all the way to Pender Street. There are many floors in the mall depending on where you are, and notable merchants include Holt Renfrew, Harry Rosen, Gap, H&M and Apple Store; the mall is connected to the Hudson'

voyage.name: Gastown
voyage.content: Is the oldest neighbourhood in Vancouver but is being reborn as a fashion and modern urban design district. Historic buildings house hip restaurants, galleries, and interior design and high-fashion shops. This area also is notable having the most tourist souvenir shops in the region.

voyage.name: Yaletown
voyage.content: Is also popular for its non-mainstream fashion boutiques and high-end salons. A few Popular Yaletown Shopping Streets are: Mainland St., Hamilton St., and Pacific Blvd.

voyage.name: Granville Island
voyage.content: Is an interesting place to go if you fancy the arts. The area boasts a public market, an art school (Emily Carr University of Art + Design), shops, a world music instrument store, restaurants, theatres, galleries, a hotel, boat docks and more.

voyage.name: Kerrisdale
voyage.content: Located in South Vancouver. Consisting of roughly a hundred or so boutique-like shops, restaurants, and stores (chain or otherwise) in an affluent neighbourhood.

voyage.name: Commercial Drive
voyage.content: Especially the stretch between 3rd Avenue and Venables St. in East Van, is great for people-watching, produce (Santa Barbara Market), cheese (La Grotta del Formaggio), sausage (JN&Z Deli), etc.

voyage.name: Main Street
voyage.content: Located in Mt Pleasant. South of Broadway stretching to around 30th Avenue, has a vibrant and expanding collection of independent restaurants, cafés, high-end niche clothing stores and small boutiques.

voyage.name: East Hastings
voyage.content: Located in East Van between Renfrew and Clark offers some of the best hidden delights in the city. There are many eclectic produce stores (Donald's Market).

voyage.name: Chinatown
voyage.content: An old historic landmark where the first Chinese immigrants to the area settled, though these days it is a shadow of its former self, having become largely deserted and full of homeless people. Other newer and more vibrant Chinatowns have sprung up around 41st Ave. and Victoria Drive, also in Richmond and Surrey, and are much better places to go to if authentic Chinese culture and food is what you are after.

voyage.name: Punjabi Market
voyage.content: Around Main, between 41st and 49th Ave. Good, cheap Punjabi food along with some Punjabi fashion; street signs are correspondingly in Punjabi.

voyage.name: Inukshuk
voyage.content: At the southern end of English Bay is this inukshuk statue facing out to sea. It's not the inukshuk statue for the Olympics; this statue was made for the city as part of Expo 86.

voyage.name: Vancouver Aquarium
voyage.content: In Stanley Park near its eastern edge. Be sure to visit the Amazon River section for some truly unusual and extraordinary animals. The last weekend in April, there is a salmon release event where you can learn about the Aquarium's new salmon breeding program and get to release and name your own fish.

voyage.name: Stanley Park Train
voyage.price: Adults $7, less for seniors, children and youth (slightly higher during special events)
voyage.content: Who doesn't like to ride a miniature railway? At Christmas, there is a very popular light display for the miniature railway.

voyage.name: Prospect Point
voyage.content: At the north tip of Stanley Park, Prospect Point affords stunning views of the Lions Gate Bridge and First Narrows. There is a concession and bathrooms here, and sometimes you may spot a large contingent of raccoons begging for food. Please don't feed them.

voyage.name: Brockton Point
voyage.content: At the north-east tip of Stanley Park, Brockton Point affords stunning views of the Lions Gate Bridge, the North Shore, and Burrard Inlet.

voyage.name: Nine O'Clock Gun
voyage.content: Built so that mariners could set their chronometers. This gun has marked 9PM every night since 1894. Also a great place to take a picture of downtown Vancouver.

voyage.name: Totem Poles
voyage.content: Near Brockton Point is this collection of eight totem poles, colourfully painted and intricately detailed.

voyage.name: Lost Lagoon
voyage.content: The place in the park to see birds, including Canada Geese, white swans, and ducks. Walking around the lagoon is a relaxing 1.8 km along paths that travel mostly near the edge of the lagoon. Feeding wildlife is no longer allowed in the park.

voyage.name: Lions Gate Bridge
voyage.content: This green coloured Vancouver landmark links the city with the North Shore across Burrard Inlet. Similar in style to San Francisco's Golden Gate Bridge, it was built in 1937-38 in large part to help develop land owned by the Guinness family (of beer fame) in West Vancouver. Although the family sold their land in the 1950s, a link remains in the decorative lighting they donated for the bridge in 1986. The bridge is th

voyage.name: Seawall
voyage.content: A paved path that begins at Canada Place in Vancouver's City Centre and follows the coast around Stanley Park through the West End and around False Creek to Granville Island and Kitsilano. It's very popular to rent bikes or rollerblades and ride/skate the piece around Stanley Park (about 9 km in length).

voyage.name: Second Beach Pool
voyage.price: Adult $4.40, children $2.25 (family entry at child rate)
voyage.content: A very large heated outdoor swimming pool. Alternatively you could swim at the beach or use the spray park near Lumberman's arch for no charge. There are lifeguards at both Second Beach and Third Beach.

voyage.name: Stanley Park Pitch & Putt
voyage.content: 18-hole course set amid rhododendron gardens. Holes range in length from 40 - 100 yards.

voyage.name: English Bay Bike Rentals
voyage.content: Offers top quality bikes at discounted prices including cruisers, city hybrids and tandem bikes in all sizes. Helmets and locks are complimentary with each rental. Children's bikes, training wheels, roller blades and dog trailers are also available. Convenient location offers easy access to the Stanley Park sea wall, Granville Island, False Creek and Science World. Call ahead to book for large groups at a discounted

voyage.name: Spokes Bicycle Rentals
voyage.price: Kids bikes starting at $4.75 an hour, Adult bikes starting at $8.57 an hour
voyage.content: Offers bike rentals and guided bike tours from a fantastic location on the doorstep of Stanley Park. Various styles of bikes for adults and children, plus helmets and locks. Weekly and monthly rates also available.

voyage.name: Celebration of Light
voyage.content: Seen one fireworks show, seen them all? Think again. Most Vancouverites come out to this event to enjoy the beach, the breeze and the hundreds of thousands of people who turn out. The fireworks themselves are just the excuse. Four shows, late July/early August. Make sure you take public transit; streets are closed and crowds are heavy.

voyage.name: Gay Pride Parade and Festival
voyage.content: Takes place on the Sunday before the first Monday in August. The parade runs along Robson Street to Denman Street to Beach Avenue, with the festival happening at Sunset Beach. This is the largest celebration of its kind in Western Canada. Parties, arts and cultural events lead up to this colourful parade and beachside festival.

voyage.name: Robson Street, primarily between Burrard St and Jervis St
voyage.content: Main shopping district downtown, Includes some of the most high-end shops in the region.

voyage.name: Cottonmouth smokeshop
voyage.content: This headshop has a vibe all unto its own. The staff and customers tend to be eccentric individuals. There is a selection of pipes, bongs and hookah equipment and supplies.

voyage.name: Stepho's Souvlaki Greek Taverna
voyage.content: A Greek restaurant in downtown Vancouver, famous for long lines of customers waiting for a table, hungry for Stepho's abundant and delicious platters of Greek favourites.

voyage.name: Whole Foods Market
voyage.content: Self service take away or eat in. A great place for vegetarians and vegans. Food is charged by weight.

voyage.name: Kintaro Ramen
voyage.content: Authentic Japanese ramen shop. Often it's crowded and there's a lineup but it moves fast. Close to Stanley Park and the bike/roller-blade rental shops on the end of Denman St.

voyage.name: Jang Mo Jib
voyage.content: Serves home style Korean food and is frequented by the local Korean students. The restaurant almost looks run-down, but it serves excellent food. Try the short ribs.

voyage.name: La Catrina
voyage.hours: Tue–Thu noon-9PM, Fri Sat 11AM-10PM, Sun 11AM-10PM, Mon closed
voyage.content: Delicious tacos, the size of the palm of your hand, topped by a variety of vegetarian or meaty options. 4-6 are usually a good meal. Bright colours and welcoming service, but only a few stools to perch on in the small space. Similar to the formula of La Pinche Taqueria in town, but cheaper.

voyage.name: Samurai Japanese Restaurant
voyage.content: Well known for having huge portions for small prices. It also has fresher sushi than some more expensive places. During meal times, it can be very difficult to get a seat. In the summer, it can be nice to get take out and walk down to Sunset Beach (4 blocks southwest on Thurlow, ~20 min). Be sure to try their toro (fatty tuna), and salmon sushi/sashimi. Stay away from their tuna sushi/sashimi because it tends to be t

voyage.name: Banana Leaf (Davie)
voyage.content: Malaysian food is a vibrant mingling of Chinese, Indian, Thai, Indonesian, and Malay, and it springs to life at Banana Leaf with rich flavours beautifully presented, yet in an efficient, low-key atmosphere. Many dishes can be prepared vegetarian. Other locations are on West Broadway (Mt Pleasant and Kits), Robson, and Denman. In location which used to be "Kam's Place", which also served southeast Asian food.

voyage.name: Kingyo
voyage.hours: Lunch 11:30AM–3PM daily; Dinner Sun–Thu 5:30–11:30PM, Fri Sat 5PM–2AM
voyage.content: Traditional izakaya dishes with a modern, fusion twist, in a decor which feels at once traditional Japanese, down-to-earth friendly, and cutting-edge. Vegetarian options available.

voyage.name: Ofra's Kitchen
voyage.content: Vividly spiced vegetarian and vegan Israeli food. Including vegan and gluten-free takes on shawarma (in pita, as a lunch sandwich) and shakshuka (with vegan sausage, and chickpeas and spinach in place of eggs).

voyage.name: Taki's Taverna
voyage.content: Another Greek taverna with long lines. A good overflow alternative to Stepho's down the block.

voyage.name: Zakkushi
voyage.content: A small Japanese restaurant that specializes in Japanese skewered meats. It would be a good idea to make a reservation.

voyage.name: Mary's on Davie
voyage.content: Mary’s on Davie (aka Hamburger Mary's) has been a fabulous food and drink destination for locals and visitors alike since 1979. Part upscale neighbourhood diner, part sassy brunch spot, and 100% part of the community, Mary’s on Davie is a place where everyone’s a little bit Mary.

voyage.name: Celebrities Nightclub
voyage.price: Cover - up to $20 (F). Drink prices vary considerably (cheaper on Tuesdays, most expensive on weekends)
voyage.content: One of Vancouver's largest clubs with varied music (DJs, house, 80s) depending on the night. Stereotype Fridays are very popular and sometimes feature international DJs. Generally a gay bar, but the crowd tends to be more mixed on Tu and F Sa.

voyage.name: The Mill Marine Bistro
voyage.content: Serves a variety of finger food, burgers, pizzas and salads with Guinness and some local brews on tap. It's a bit overpriced, but the patio (on the park looking at the harbour) is hard to beat.

voyage.name: HI Vancouver (Downtown)
voyage.content: A location of the Hostelling International chain, this is a rather nice and very clean hostel. Games room, a spacious kitchen, TV room, internet access, free breakfast. It's a little far from downtown walking-wise, but located on a very nice, quiet street near the waterfront.

voyage.name: Buchan Hotel
voyage.price: $80-140, with cheaper rates mid-Oct to March
voyage.content: B&B style hotel in a West End residential area. Some rooms have private baths while others have shared facilities. No parking available if you have a car.

voyage.name: The Listel Hotel
voyage.content: Boutique hotel with an arts twist -- a number of the rooms and floors have been decorated by local museums or artists.

voyage.name: The Sylvia Hotel
voyage.price: $115-200 (May - mid-Oct), cheaper rates available in low season
voyage.content: Hotel in a heritage building across the street from English Bay Beach. Mixture of standard rooms and suites, some rooms have a kitchen.

voyage.name: Times Square Suites
voyage.content: Apartment-style suites with a full kitchen, DVD, washer/dryer and fireplace. A little pricey, but for the location (literally two blocks from Lost Lagoon, and two blocks to shopping on Robson Street) it's worth it.

voyage.name: Westin Bayshore Resort & Marina
voyage.content: Luxury resort next to the Stanley Park with 510 rooms and stunning views of Coal Harbour and mountains.

voyage.name: Bill Reid Gallery of Northwest Coast Art
voyage.content: The Gallery showcases the permanent collection of acclaimed Haida artist Bill Reid (1920–1998) and changing exhibitions of contemporary Northwest Coast Art. Gallery highlights include over 40 pieces of Bill Reid’s gold and silver jewelry, Reid’s bronze masterpiece Mythic Messengers, several of Reid’s works that were featured on the Canadian $20 bill and a full-scale totem pole, carved by James Hart of Haida Gwaii.

voyage.name: Jack Poole Plaza
voyage.content: Brick-paved plaza with good views of the North Shore mountains, Stanley Park and Coal Harbour. It is also the home of the Olympic Cauldron.

voyage.name: Library Square and Vancouver Public Library
voyage.content: The modern and attractive central branch of the City of Vancouver's Public Library is located in an architecturally interesting building, designed by Moshe Safdie. Constructed as a 'square within a circle', this building is reminiscent of a modern Roman Colosseum. Its design was chosen in a public competition. There are large public spaces around the building and a nice atrium space in the lobby. Guest internet acces

voyage.name: Robson Square
voyage.price: Skating is available during winter and is free, skate rentals are $3
voyage.content: Both an office building and public space designed by Vancouver architect Arthur Erikson, it houses the Provincial Courts and a satellite UBC campus. The building, which was built to represent a skyscraper on its side, is noted for its use of water and greenery and is mostly underground. The public space features a skating rink underneath Robson Street, which is the only outdoor rink in Vancouver.

voyage.name: Vancouver Art Gallery
voyage.content: You can see and learn a lot about Emily Carr in the permanent collection, but the rest of the gallery varies in quality depending on what they have been able to attract as special exhibits. Take advantage of admission by donation on Tuesday (5-9PM) and sample what is there before paying the full admission.

voyage.name: Vancouver Lookout
voyage.price: $18.25, discounts for children, seniors and students available; best prices if bought at Tourism Vancouver office
voyage.content: Located on the top floor of the Harbour Centre, the Lookout offers a full 360-degree panoramic view of the city from 130 m up. You'll see the downtown area, Stanley Park, the North Shore mountains and even the skyline of nearby Burnaby. The ticket is good for two trips during the day, so you can see it in the daytime and return for the sunset view.

voyage.name: Canada Place
voyage.content: Built for Expo 86 as Canada's exhibit, today the building serves as a cruise ship terminal and the eastern building of Vancouver Convention Centre. It is also the site of an IMAX theatre and the luxurious Pan Pacific Hotel. Walk around the unique sailed structure and take in views of the building itself, Coal Harbour, and the North Shore. It uses white colour with a roof of funky "sails" or "waves", which is a curved

voyage.name: Christ Church Cathedral
voyage.content: Vancouver's oldest surviving church was completed in 1889. Often in the shadow of its neighbour, the 23-storey Cathedral Place, you should visit in the afternoon to see the sun shining through the stained glass windows.

voyage.name: Marine Building
voyage.content: This 22-storey Art Deco office tower was completed in 1930. Because of the Great Depression, only four floors were occupied for the first several years. Note the attention to detail on both the exterior, and in the lobby.

voyage.name: Hotel Vancouver
voyage.content: The third such hotel in this spot, the Hotel Vancouver was built over 11 years and completed in 1939. As with all Canadian Pacific hotels in Canada, the chateau-style is truly impressive. It was the tallest building in Vancouver until 1972. The hotel's first guests were King George and Queen Elizabeth. Bring binoculars for a close-up view of the building's many gargoyles.

voyage.name: One Wall Centre
voyage.content: Voted the world's best new skyscraper in 2001 by Emporis.

voyage.name: Telus Garden
voyage.content: Glass office building with a distinct outside that contains 4 storey gardens.

voyage.name: Vancouver House
voyage.content: A neo-futurist residential skyscraper with 49 floors. Its base is a triangle, that gradually changes into a rectangle - giving it a very uncanny/slim shape from some angles.

voyage.name: Vancouver Opera
voyage.content: Offers world-class performances from some of the world's best composers. The listed address is the ticket office, which is not in Vancouver's downtown. Most performances take place at Queen Elizabeth Theatre, which hosts a variety of entertainment performances in the downtown area.

voyage.name: Vancouver Symphony Orchestra
voyage.content: A great night out at reasonable prices. Students can purchase $10 tickets with the VSO Access Pass. Concerts generally take place at the Orpheum at the noted address.

voyage.name: Long Table Distillery Ltd.
voyage.content: A craft distillery of vodkas, gins, and other spirits, many of which bubble in the back room. Free tastings are offered on a 14-foot recovered-tree "long table" in the front room. If your only experience of gin and vodka comes from uninspiring mass-market pap, you are in for a treat. The friendly staff love explaining the finer points of which aromatics go in which chamber of their gleaming, copper 300-litre still. O
On April 20th people congregate at the Vancouver Art Gallery to smoke marijuana and celebrate this unofficial holiday, a reflection of BC's relaxed attitudes towards cannabis.

voyage.name: Canada Day at Canada Place
voyage.content: A large, engaging, though somewhat corporate celebration of Canada's national holiday. The citizenship ceremony can be moving. There are usually several bands, fun activities for the kids, and exhibits of Canadian Forces and other bits of Canadiana.

voyage.name: Canada Day Fireworks
voyage.price: Free viewing from streets, premium Canada Place seating for a fee
voyage.content: There is a fireworks display after dark on Canada Day.

voyage.name: Vancouver Zombie Walk
voyage.content: Usually either in the summer or near Halloween, anyone can choose to dress up and act as the living dead during this parade through Downtown. Although this has only been in Vancouver for about 2 years, thousands of people have already participated, and at least 500 people each year join in on this zombie walk. It is free, and mostly for plain fun, and is also an unofficial event. Each year, there is a set meeting spo

voyage.name: Pacific Centre
voyage.content: Has more than 150 shops, restaurants and services if you want to walk in an underground shopping centre. The shopping centre begins at its north end at Robson Street, and stretches all the way to Pender Street. There are many floors in the mall depending on where you are, and notable merchants include Holt Renfrew, Harry Rosen, Gap, H&M and Apple Store; the mall is connected to Vancouver Centre (a small mall mainly c

voyage.name: Robson Street, primarily between Burrard St and Jervis St
voyage.content: Main shopping district downtown, it includes some of the most high-end shops in the region.

voyage.name: H-Mart
voyage.content: Hidden on the second floor is a large grocery store featuring a wide range of high-quality, primarily Korean groceries. Part of a North American chain of Korean stores. The food court offers a number of good lunch choices, too.

voyage.name: Cannabis Culture
voyage.content: The BCMP "Bookstore" is a centre of the marijuana subculture of Vancouver. It is the party headquarters for the provincial marijuana party as well as a store and lounge. Proceeds from the BCMP go towards the party and the legal battle against the extradition of the party leader who faces life in prison in the USA. The front half of the store is taken up by display shelves of bongs, pipes, rolling papers and pretty mu

voyage.name: New Amsterdam Café
voyage.content: The New Amsterdam Café, directly next door to the BCMP Bookstore, permits the smoking of marijuana. The Amsterdam offers a friendly environment to meet new people and to exercise some of the more unique freedoms that Vancouver offers. While it is not, however, generally permitted to buy or sell marijuana on or near the premises, it is not policed or enforced, so long as it in the spirit of sharing, within reason. The

voyage.name: Roots
voyage.content: Their fashionable designs with motifs of beavers, maple leaves, and canoes gave rise to what has been called "Roots nationalism", a kind of branded Canadian pride. There are several stores for this brand of clothing, bags and shoes in Vancouver, but if you're looking for a Canadian souvenir that is less obviously touristy, or are from the part of the world where the word "roots" with a picture of a beaver is a double

voyage.name: Wildlife Thrift Store
voyage.content: A large variety of clothes and household items for cheap. They donate their proceeds to local charities.

voyage.name: Breka Bakery & Café
voyage.content: Open 24/7 at all 7 locations, with 4 located downtown. Very large, very fresh selection of baked goods. All made locally, and then baked on site. Add-ons like oat, almond, soy milk and flavour shots are free. Limited selection of gluten-free and vegan options. All downtown locations are lively: limited seating during peak hours. Fanciest interior is at the newest location on Hastings St.

voyage.name: Caffè Artigiano
voyage.content: Excellent coffee shop featuring "latte art," but it's still great. IntelligentsiA coffee available. Great espresso. This small chain has a total of four locations in this district, plus other locations in the Lower Mainland and Calgary.

voyage.name: Cartems Donuterie
voyage.content: They modestly claim the title of "best donuts in Vancouver". They certainly have some of the most interesting flavours. Try the "whiskey bacon" donut. Also coffee and tea, served with a friendly smile in a hip setting.

voyage.name: European Breads
voyage.content: An organic crêpes café, which also sells various freshly-baked breads of organic wheat, rye, spelt, and other grains. Well set up for a light breakfast, lunch, or snack. Free wifi.

voyage.name: Fritz Frie House
voyage.content: This restaurant boasts what one of the best poutines in town. The curds are imported from Quebec. The garlic lover's mayo is fantastic too. Cleverly located next to the local Fitness World. $5 for a medium. Open until the wee hours in the morning, frequented by nightclubbers. Regularly wins local awards for fries.

voyage.name: Japadog
voyage.content: A Vancouver street food icon that now has its own shop. It's a twist on the traditional hot dog with your choice of pork, turkey or bratwurst smothered in Japanese flavours and toppings like seaweed, miso glaze, Japanese chilli and teriyaki sauce. There are also several Japadog carts around downtown, some with a kobe beef option. Look for the carts on Burrard St and in front of Waterfront Station.

voyage.name: Mink, A Chocolate Café
voyage.content: The coffee is strong, the hot chocolate is rich and the chocolate is plentiful. Dairy-free available. Waffles and fruit parfaits. The chocolate fondue with pound cake and seasonal fruit for dipping is excellent (just make sure there's at least two of you to share!). As a chocolate maker, they use their own chocolate in everything. Large selection of house-made chocolate bars, bonbons, & confections for retail.

voyage.name: Pita Wrap Café
voyage.content: The usual falafels, souvlakis, shawarmas and Greek plates, but very well executed.

voyage.name: Tree's Organic Coffee & Roasting House
voyage.content: A coffeehouse featuring carefully selected, 100% certified organic, coffee. Justifiably proud of its reaaaally good cheesecake. This is the flagship of a small local chain; there are other locations in Yaletown, Gastown and Richmond.

voyage.name: Vancouver Community College Cafeteria
voyage.content: The cafeteria is run by the culinary arts program so you get gourmet food at cafeteria prices. Usually have a large seafood selection. Don't miss the Asian Food program which has a separate service area. As you would expect from students, the quality can vary. However, it is hard to complain when you get a fancy meal for less than $8.

voyage.name: Kamei Royal
voyage.content: This is the Japanese restaurant to which you can bring your homesick Japanese business partners. Excellently prepared, professional-grade sushi, rice dishes, kushiyaki, and cooked-at-the-table sukiyaki. An authentic Japanese atmosphere, from the irasshaimase greeting to the pretty pictures in the bilingual menus to the serene decor. Tucked above a Tiffany's store on the second floor, you look out over the crowds on G

voyage.name: Medina Café
voyage.hours: Mon-Fri 8AM-4PM, Sat Sun 9AM-4PM. Weekend brunch served 9AM-3PM
voyage.content: Menu includes Moroccan-influenced dishes, fricasse (fried eggs with braised short ribs) and Belgian waffles with a choice of unusual sauces like milk chocolate lavender and white chocolate pistachio rosewater, plus many other breakfast and lunch concoctions. It seats about 75 or so, but lineups and long waits are still normal, especially for brunch on weekends.

voyage.name: Shabusen Yakiniku House
voyage.content: A Japanese and Korean BBQ House specializing in a large all-you-can-eat menu. Fun part of eating here is that you can order raw meat and cook it yourself on the grill installed at the table. There is another location in South Granville.

voyage.name: Coast
voyage.content: Fresh seafood from coastal regions throughout the world. Try the Chef's Community Table, where the chef prepares the food for up to 14 diners right at the table.

voyage.name: Hy's Steakhouse & Cocktail Bar
voyage.content: The most amazing service in Vancouver. Classy steakhouse that has been serving Vancouver for some fifty years. Charcoal steaks are the house specialty, but the menu also includes local cuisine like Pacific Salmon and Ahi Tuna. The servers do an incredible job and the food is excellent.

voyage.name: Joe Forte's Seafood & Chop House
voyage.price: With glamour comes a price; expect to spend about $70/person for a complete dinner
voyage.content: Open daily for lunch and dinner; reservations strongly recommended. Usually mentioned amongst the top 5 restaurants in Vancouver, here you will find great food and great service. In the lavishly decorated open space, you may even catch a glimpse of a celebrity as you savour the oysters that are a specialty here.

voyage.name: Miku
voyage.content: Japanese restaurant that specializes in aburi (seared on the outside while raw inside). There's also a small bar at the entrance.

voyage.name: Commodore Ballroom
voyage.content: This is a large venue frequent location for live concerts. Has a large famous 'sprung' dance floor. Capacity is 900 people. On most nights, tickets are required to get in.

voyage.name: The Railway Stage & Beer Cafe
voyage.content: Popular bar that frequently features live music. The crowd is a mix of ages, although probably more over 30. It's not a big place, so it gets packed easily. There are more tables at the other end of the long bar if you want to sit down and talk.

voyage.name: The Roxy
voyage.content: Long-time Vancouver club which features top 40 rock. The house band, Loaded/Fully Loaded, covers some of the best of the recent pop and rock M-Sa, with country music on Sunday.

voyage.name: Ambassador Hotel
voyage.content: A boutique-style hotel with single, twin, double and queen rooms. Washrooms are shared (per floor) but are private upon entry.

voyage.name: Cambie Hostel - Downtown
voyage.price: Dorms start at $27, or $24 with Cambie Card

voyage.name: SameSun Vancouver
voyage.price: Dorms start at $35, private rooms at $85
voyage.content: Hostel with modern amenities and decorated by bright splashes of colours on the wall.

voyage.name: Best Western Plus Chateau Granville
voyage.content: Rooms and suites with tea/coffee maker, microwave, and refrigerator. Exterior of building is unattractive, but rooms are pleasant. Surrounding area still in the process of being gentrified.

voyage.name: The Burrard
voyage.content: Old motor inn remodelled to go for the funky factor. Some of the rooms are small and its age still shows in spots, but there's lots of character, free wifi, new beds and mini-fridges and espresso machines in each room.

voyage.name: Days Inn Vancouver Downtown
voyage.content: It's an old building so some of the rooms are small and noisy. Otherwise, a typical Days Inn - clean, simple rooms, but not many extras. Free wireless Internet available.

voyage.name: GEC Granville Hotel
voyage.content: Mix of rooms with single queen, single king, two double beds or two queen beds.

voyage.name: Kingston Hotel
voyage.content: Single rooms have a 3/4 double bed and shared washroom facilities. Twin and double rooms have their own washrooms. Comes with a free continental breakfast.

voyage.name: L'Hermitage
voyage.content: Boutique-style hotel in a condo tower. Room options range from "Boutique" rooms that have a queen or king-size bed to one and two bedroom suites for extended stays. Amenities include a fitness room, heated outdoor saltwater pool and complementary wifi.

voyage.name: Ramada Vancouver Hotel
voyage.content: Accommodation includes full hot breakfast, adjacent fitness centre, business centre, guest laundry/dry cleaning service, 24-hr concierge, complimentary wifi and baggage storage. The hotel is pet-friendly and also has an on-site bar and lounge. Some rooms have kitchenettes.

voyage.name: Victorian Hotel
voyage.content: One of Vancouver's first guest houses, the hotel retains a lot of its original woodwork and Victorian-era details. Economy rooms have one or two beds and a sink, with a shared bathroom. Luxury rooms have one to three beds and full bathroom. There is complementary continental breakfast and wifi; secure parking is available for a fee.

voyage.name: Atrium Hotel Vancouver
voyage.content: Ideally located in Vancouver’s East Village, right across from the PNE, our hotel offers newly renovated, cozy rooms designed for comfort and value. Enjoy a complimentary breakfast and free parking, all just an 8-minute walk from the Coliseum—perfect for catching concerts and games. With quick, easy access to downtown, it's your affordable home base for exploring the city.

voyage.name: Exchange Hotel Vancouver
voyage.content: Opened in 2018 in the former stock exchange building.

voyage.name: Fairmont Hotel Vancouver
voyage.content: Vancouver's grand old hotel. Beautifully decorated and a firmly established part of Vancouver's history. The lounge is noted for its traditional afternoon tea.

voyage.name: The Fairmont Waterfront
voyage.content: A 5-star hotel with a stunning view wherever there's a window. Across from Canada Place.

voyage.name: Hotel Le Soleil
voyage.content: Suites and guestrooms with luxury touches like marble bathrooms and unique artwork and decor from local artisans and the Old World. Rated "One of the Top 100 Hotels in the World" - by Resorts & Great Hotels Magazine.

voyage.name: Loden Hotel
voyage.price: From $279. Additional fee for valet parking, internet access $15/day
voyage.content: Has the modern look and feel with earthy tones, deep soaker tubs and a yoga studio. There's also a 24 hour fitness centre and free bike rentals. The floor to ceiling windows provide good harbour or city views (depending on which way your room faces).

voyage.name: Marriott Pinnacle Downtown Hotel
voyage.content: A good weddings and meetings hotel steps away from the harbour and cruise ship terminal. Fitness centre, indoor lap pool and whirlpool.

voyage.name: The Metropolitan
voyage.content: Luxury hotel featuring marble washrooms and soaker tubs.

voyage.name: Pan Pacific Vancouver
voyage.content: This modern hotel consists of an array of modern furnished luxury rooms and suites.

voyage.name: Rosewood Hotel Georgia
voyage.content: A historic Vancouver hotel where the rich and the royal have stayed in the past. Those guests have moved on but the hotel retains a mix of elegant rooms and suites. Amenities include a fitness centre and indoor saltwater pool.

voyage.name: Shangri-La Hotel
voyage.content: A luxury hotel located in the tallest building in Vancouver with 119 guest rooms, executive suites and space for meetings and events. Rooms include marble bathrooms, PVRs and floor to ceiling windows to take in the marvellous view. Other amenities include a 24 hour health club, outdoor pool and access to the Chi spa. The hotel also offers MARKET by Jean-Georges, Jean-Georges Vongerichten's Canadian debut.

voyage.name: Sutton Place Hotel
voyage.content: Classic-styled luxury hotel with spa, gym, concierge and the usual room amenities. Reviewers like the ambiance, the friendly staff and the location, but find the WiFi signal weak and thought some of the furnishings looked a bit dated.

voyage.name: Wedgewood Hotel and Spa
voyage.content: European-style boutique hotel listed on Conde Nast's gold list. The decor isn't modern but reviewers like the elegance and class of the hotel and found the rooms well appointed and comfortable. Amenities include a spa and fitness centre and business centre for internet access (no wifi in rooms).

voyage.name: Gastown
voyage.content: The oldest part of downtown. You will find cobble-paved boulevards and over-priced tourist traps selling every imaginable thing you can print "Vancouver" on. Popular with tourists are the Gastown Steam Clock, promoted as the only active steam clock in the world but in fact an electric clock that pumps steam, rather an underwhelming experience. The area is notorious for aggressive beggars-drug addicts who are quite un

voyage.name: Dominion Building
voyage.content: A distinctive red and mustard coloured building completed in 1910. It was the first steel-framed high-rise built in Vancouver and briefly was the tallest commercial building in the British Empire.

voyage.name: Chinatown Millennium Gate
voyage.content: Located at the western edge of Chinatown, it consists of ornamental arches with tiled roofs in traditional Chinese style.

voyage.name: Dr. Sun Yat-Sen Classical Chinese Garden
voyage.content: A Ming-dynasty style garden in Chinatown. Built in 1986 by Chinese craftsmen using traditional materials, tools, and techniques, this was the first classical garden built outside China. The gardens combine traditional Chinese buildings, plants, a small lake, and curved footpaths to create the illusion of a very big place within a single block. Tours are available. Compared to the city park next door, the differences

voyage.name: Dr. Sun Yat-Sen Park
voyage.content: Constructed by Vancouver-area designers at the same time as its classical garden neighbour, this public park shares the lake and the Chinese garden look. But this is a city park, and free to enter.

voyage.name: Gastown Steam Clock
voyage.content: A clock that tries to look old and belches steam every 15 minutes may not be the most stunning landmark, but it has an endearing charm in a kitschy kind of way. It was built to take advantage of the steam vents that are all over downtown Vancouver, but it never lived up to its billing and now relies on electricity to count the minutes. It is one of a kind though and remains a photographic pilgrimage for thousands of

voyage.name: Sam Kee Building
voyage.content: This two-storey building is the world's narrowest commercial building according to the Guinness Book of World Records, with a width of just 4'11" (1.5 m) at its base. Its slim size is due to the city expropriating most of the lot to widen the street. The owner went ahead and built anyway, and businesses have been operating out of its confines since 1913. If you do take a look, the perspective is better from the other

voyage.name: Sun Tower
voyage.content: A high-rise building built in the Beaux-Arts style. It was completed in 1912 and was the tallest building in the British Empire at the time. The tower is noted for its dome (painted to look like copper cladding) and its exterior was used in the TV series, Smallville.

voyage.name: Vancouver Police Museum
voyage.content: Exhibits on the history of Vancouver's police, unusual weapons that have been confiscated and notable Vancouver crimes. There are also a number of programs and activities geared towards kids.

voyage.name: Victory Square
voyage.content: A small park covering one city block. It has the cenotaph commemorating the dead from World War I and is the site of Vancouver's Remembrance Day ceremonies.

voyage.name: Chinese New Year
voyage.content: Because there is such a strong Chinese population in the city, the Lunar New Year period is often one of the most exciting and colourful in the city. There is usually a parade in Chinatown and many of the public schools usually have a day off on Chinese New Year. You can also catch celebrations at Tinseltown mall (1 minute from Stadium Skytrain station), and in Richmond at the International Buddhist Temple. There, vi

voyage.name: Chinatown
voyage.content: A great place for shopping for groceries and some Asian products. Located primarily between Columbia St to the west, East Pender St to the north, Gore Ave to the east, and East Georgia St to the south.

voyage.name: Oomomo
voyage.content: This Japanese dollar store is the anchor of the International Village Shopping Centre. Has a surprisingly diverse (candy, kitchen supplies, stationary, electronics, etc.) selection of cute Japanese things. A fun browse.

voyage.name: Chinatown Night Market
voyage.content: Styled after Asian marketplaces these very popular nights have all kinds of stuff for sale. Watch out for the cheap imitation knock-offs that are commonly available.

voyage.name: The Chinese Tea Shop
voyage.content: Visit the specialty tea boutique, to purchase specialty teas such as oolong, green, white tea, black and pu-erh, as well as learn about the finer points of Gong Fu Cha and tea culture.

voyage.name: John Fluevog
voyage.content: A shoe shop with interesting architecture that is built with glass panels between the two walls of an alleyway. Fine shoes.

voyage.name: Roden Gray
voyage.content: Boutique selling high-fashion goods.

voyage.name: Meat & Bread
voyage.content: Simple menu but good food. There are four sandwiches, mostly focusing on roasted or braised meat (the Porchetta is the signature sandwich), and two sides that change daily. The bread is pretty dense but the portion of meat is generous so it's a filling meal. To finish it off (if you have room), you can get a bowl of Maple Bacon ice cream. The ambiance is interesting as well, with a couple of long tables for seating..

voyage.name: Old Spaghetti Factory
voyage.content: Spaghetti and other standard Italian dishes, but well-priced and has sidewalk seating.

voyage.name: Phnom Penh
voyage.content: Very popular restaurant tucked away on a side street in Chinatown that has been winning local readers choice awards for 20 years. The menu is Vietnamese and Cambodian with a large number of dishes. The deep-fried chicken wings and butter beef (similar to beef carpaccio but slightly more cooked, with soy sauce and cilantro) are both very tasty and amongst the most popular dishes. Portions are a good size and in line w

voyage.name: Save On Meats
voyage.content: Diner-style restaurant that does simple comfort food well. Breakfast menu includes three egg omelettes and eggs benedict; lunch/dinner menu has sandwiches, some entrees and possibly the best burger value in Vancouver (bacon and cheeseburger with fries for $7). Full breakfast menu is served until 11AM on weekdays and 4PM on weekends. Eggs are available all day.

voyage.name: Steamworks
voyage.content: Long-standing brew pub that is popular with locals and tourists. There's a patio and restaurant at street level; pool tables and bar downstairs. The menu is extensive with pub standards like burgers and nachos, but also includes steaks, seafood and pasta.

voyage.name: The Irish Heather
voyage.content: Nice atmosphere, excellent pheasant, and apparently the only place in Vancouver that serves real Guinness.

voyage.name: Waffleland Café
voyage.content: Delicious Belgian and Norwegian style waffles, sweet and savoury. Excellent vegetarian and vegan options.

voyage.name: Al Porto
voyage.content: Nice Mediterranean-themed decor with a variety of pizza, pasta, seafood and meat dishes.

voyage.name: Chambar
voyage.content: Belgian restaurant with mussels and a variety of meat dishes on the menu. A small but delicious selection of vegetarian options. The beer list includes over 25 beers from Belgium. Wide selection of wines. Save room for the fascinating desserts. Don't be surprised if the general manager is the one who takes your empty plates; they are that involved. Exquisite food plus excellent service equals one of the best dining e

voyage.name: Water Street Cafe
voyage.content: Elegant restaurant known for its pasta and seafood dishes.

voyage.name: Wildebeest
voyage.price: Plates range from $3-42, with most between $10-20
voyage.content: A restaurant with some unique menu items that draw rave reviews from many but claims of being overhyped from others. The menu is meat-centric with dishes from varying parts of the animal — think pork jowls with oats, bone marrow, beef cheeks, as well as more traditional cuts like rib eye and roast chicken breasts. The restaurant makes good use of its Gastown location with brick walls and wooden tables and follows cur

voyage.name: Guilt and Company
voyage.content: Creative and artsy sort of bar. Features some unique beers on tap and a selection of board games; order cheese from the bar and play some giant Jenga. Often features indie rock performances.

voyage.name: Lamplighter
voyage.content: One part sports bar and one part club gives this bar a dual personality which works for some and not for others. The crowd is a more mixed and mellow than Shine or Fabric.

voyage.name: MIA Nightclub
voyage.content: Smallish dance club with a variety of music, depending on the night.

voyage.name: The Alibi Room
voyage.content: Offers an array of microbrews with an emphasis on British Columbia breweries, as well as a diverse food menu.

voyage.name: The Black Frog
voyage.hours: Mon-Thu 11:30AM-1AM, Fri 11:30AM-2AM, Sat noon-2AM, Sun noon-midnight
voyage.content: Smallish pub with some character. Good spot for pre-activity drinks or if you want somewhere not as loud. Also has a small but well prepared selection of burgers, sandwiches and fish and chips that are an excellent value.

voyage.name: The Blarney Stone
voyage.content: Bit of an Irish bar, bit of a dance club. Attracts a 20-something crowd most nights. Irish showband Killarney are a regular feature.

voyage.name: The Cambie
voyage.content: Frontier-looking unpretentious bar with well-worn wooden benches and tables. Popular with the younger crowd and the nearby backpackers hostel. Lots of rock music and no dance floor. Pitchers are amongst the cheapest in Vancouver.

voyage.name: Columbia Hotel
voyage.content: Hostel accommodations in an old historical building in the middle of Gastown.

voyage.name: Patricia Hotel
voyage.content: Very basic hotel that is a good option if you want something cheap and don't mind a small room in a bad part of town. The rooms are tidy and come with small TVs and private bathrooms. Wifi is available but signal strength varies. Room options range from Budget and Basic rooms with one double bed to Quad Rooms with two queen beds and views of the city. There is a pub on the ground floor that sometimes has live music.

voyage.name: St Clair Hotel Hostel
voyage.content: The hotel-hostel is a heritage-listed building, built-in 1911 by Captain Henry Pybus and architect Samuel Birds. It was the first concrete building in Vancouver, and was built as accommodation for railway and ocean-going passengers from both Pacific and Atlantic locations. The nautical theme has been preserved.

voyage.name: BC Place
voyage.content: The home of the BC Lions CFL football team and Vancouver Whitecaps FC in Major League Soccer. It also hosts the Canada Sevens, a major international event in the sevens variant of men's rugby union. The building is also home to many conventions, tradeshows and concerts. It has had two roofs in its history, both claimed as the largest of their types in the world. The original roof was air-supported, but it has since b

voyage.name: BC Lions
voyage.content: The local Canadian Football League (CFL) team. The regular season is June to October. Playoff are in November.

voyage.name: Vancouver Whitecaps FC
voyage.content: The local Major League Soccer (MLS) team. The regular season is from February to October. Playoff are from October to December.

voyage.name: Rogers Arena
voyage.content: The building also hosts many of the big name concerts that come to Vancouver.

voyage.name: Vancouver Canucks
voyage.content: The local National Hockey League (NHL) team. The regular season runs from October until early April. Playoffs last until June. Games are usually good entertainment. However, tickets and food/drink are expensive, and tickets can be hard to get if the team is having an average or better season.

voyage.name: Olympic Village
voyage.content: The site of the Vancouver Athletes Village during the 2010 Winter Olympic Games. It's slowly being sold off as condos and becoming a community within Vancouver. The central plaza is distinctive with the deep red of the Salt Building and the giant sparrow statues. There is also a terraced slope leading down to False Creek that is lovely for sitting in the sun.

voyage.name: Roundhouse Community Center
voyage.content: The restored roundhouse that used to work the railyard before the condos were built. Engine 374, which hauled the first passengers into Vancouver, is on display with some historical information. There is also a gym that can be used on a drop-in basis (for a small fee) and a small performing arts centre.

voyage.name: Science World
voyage.price: $30.40 per adult, $24.30 for 13-18 years old and 65+, $20.30 for 3-12 years old, free for 2 years old and younger
voyage.content: This science centre is located in the distinctive building from Expo 86 at the end of False Creek. Has a wide range of participatory exhibits. Get off the Skytrain at the Main St/Science World station. The building is a unique shaped building that was constructed for Expo 86. Popular with the young and with those who like science. An Omnimax theatre is in this building as well.

voyage.name: JV Bike
voyage.price: $10-16 for first hour (depends on the type of bike) and $5-8 for each additional hour. $40-60 for 24 hours. Additional charge for trailers
voyage.content: Bicycle shop that also rents bikes, including tandem bikes and electric assist bikes to make the hills a little easier. Options to rent hourly, or daily up to a week.

voyage.name: Marinaside Crescent
voyage.content: Located about south 300 m south of the station.

voyage.name: Mountain Equipment Company
voyage.content: A popular store for outdoors supplies.

voyage.name: Fuse Pan-Asian Express
voyage.price: Tapas, salads $3-7, stir-fried to order $8, Grilled items $6-12
voyage.hours: Coffee & self-serve 9AM onward daily; Full menu Mon-Fri 11AM-8PM; Sat Sun Hols noon-6PM
voyage.content: A fusion of several Asian cuisines, and a fusion of the virtues of prompt service and good food. Except for the grab-and-go items, everything is made to order with house-made sauces. There is a respectable vegetarian selection. Free parking, and an easy walk from Yaletown offices or the Roundhouse. Phone in advanced orders.

voyage.name: Glowbal grill & satay bar
voyage.hours: afternoon menu 3PM-5PM daily, dinner 5PM-Midnight daily; Mon-Fri lunch 11:30AM-3PM; Sat Sun brunch 10:30AM-3PM
voyage.content: Glowbal is a trendy hit in the heart of the Yaletown restaurant row. Brunches are famous, but dinners are also outstanding. Don't be surprised if the chef stops by to offer some custom-made treat if the menu doesn't suffice, and expect the flavours to be marvellous. Attentive, friendly, and uniformly black-clad service. A top-notch operation in every way. Valet parking Thursday-Saturday nights.

voyage.name: Terra Breads Cafe
voyage.content: Bakery and cafe known for its artisan breads baked in a stone hearth oven. Serves a selection of salads, sandwiches and hot plates for lunch, plus a small breakfast menu. Sandwiches/paninis are made with their own bread, and include tasty options like roast lamb on fig and anise bread and roast turkey on cranberry pistachio bread.

voyage.name: Yaletown Brewing Company
voyage.content: Popular brewpub in the heart of Yaletown.

voyage.name: Blue Water Cafe
voyage.content: Arguably Vancouver's premier upscale destination for seafood, Blue Water offers fine dining, drinking, and a raw bar. The seafood preparations are direct, emphasizing fresh, flavorful ingredients over showy virtuoso techniques, and many are Japanese-influenced. The wine and cocktail lists are also exceptional. A few non-seafood items (including a couple of vegetarian friendly options) make it possible to bring a grou

voyage.name: The London Public House
voyage.content: Imported & craft beers, pub food, but it's not a great place to walk at night, as that section is not far removed from the worst areas of the Eastside.

voyage.name: Capo and the Spritz
voyage.content: Bar/lounge inside the much-hyped Opus Hotel in Yaletown.

voyage.name: C&N Backpackers Hostel
voyage.price: $25 for a dorm room, $55 for a double room
voyage.content: Hostel with dorm rooms (3 or 4 beds) and double rooms. Also offers bike rentals, free Wifi and will arrange pub crawls.

voyage.name: C&N Central Station Hostel
voyage.price: $25 for a dorm room, $55 for a private room
voyage.content: Second location for C&N.

voyage.name: Hampton Inn & Suites
voyage.price: From $249 (parking is an extra $19 + tax per night)
voyage.content: Rooms come with two queen beds or a king bed. Suite options are also available. Amenities include free hot breakfast, free Wifi, free bike rentals, a free shuttle service to downtown (operates between 7AM and 8PM) and gym/fitness center with sauna and whirlpool.

voyage.name: Opus Hotel
voyage.price: From $300 in summer, from $200 other times
voyage.content: Stylish hotel in Yaletown that has made it to Conde Nast's gold list four years running. Reviewers like the modern decor and friendly staff but don't recommend it for families. Perks include free bike rentals, free in-room iPad and free Wifi.

voyage.name: YWCA Hotel
voyage.price: Summer rates range from $73-90 (single room) and $90-133 (double room)
voyage.content: A modern hotel with a range of room sizes and prices. Close walk to most attractions and near BC Place Stadium. All rooms are private but some have shared bathrooms.

voyage.name: JW Marriott Parq Vancouver
voyage.content: A four star hotel opened in September 2017, right next to BC Place.

voyage.name: Irving K. Barber Learning Centre
voyage.content: This library has the Automated Storage and Retrieval System (ASRS), an automated "robot librarian" cranes scurry along 5-story shelves holding 1.6 million books, at the beck and call of human librarians. For a geek thrill, watch them through the ground floor windows on the north side of the building. On the 2nd floor, near the Circulation desk, is a more limited view.

voyage.name: Beaty Biodiversity Museum
voyage.content: Home to Canada's largest blue whale skeleton, a herbarium, and a wide array of animal specimens including fish, insects, arthropods, tetrapods, marine invertebrates and fossils.

voyage.name: Chan Centre for the Performing Arts
voyage.content: A concert hall and events centre; often the location of convocation ceremonies.

voyage.name: Morris and Helen Belkin Art Gallery
voyage.hours: Tue-Fri 10AM-5PM, Sat Sun noon-5PM (closed Mondays and statutory holidays)
voyage.content: A small gallery with regular exhibitions. What looks like a woodpile outside is actually a sculpture, made of concrete.

voyage.name: Nitobe Memorial Garden
voyage.content: One of the most traditional, authentic Japanese gardens in North America and among the top five Japanese gardens outside of Japan.

voyage.name: UBC Botanical Garden
voyage.price: $7 (discounts available), audioguide $3. Free for UBC students, and faculty, staff, or neighbours holding a Garden Pass
voyage.content: Canada's longest continuously operating university garden, it contains over 8000 different kinds of plants in both designed landscapes and coastal forest settings. Must-sees are the Asian garden, the alpine garden and the food garden. An enchanting oasis. Compared to the more-visited Van Dusen Botanical Garden, the remoteness of the garden means fewer people and a quieter, more private setting. Guided tours free with

voyage.name: UBC Museum of Anthropology
voyage.price: $15.68 adults, $13.44 students/seniors, children 6 and under free ($7.84 flat rate Tu 5-9PM)
voyage.content: Devoted to world cultures, but with an emphasis on the First Nations of the Northwest Coast. Includes a splendid collection of totem poles, a mind-boggling array of artifacts from around the world, and a number of changing exhibits.

voyage.name: Jericho Beach
voyage.content: Is a more family oriented sandy beach with a large picnicking area. The beach forms a crescent shape which creates a sheltered swimming area that is relatively shallow. In the summer, the beach is patrolled by lifeguards who monitor beach near the floating dock. Jericho Beach is also a great location to go windsurfing or dinghy sailing.

voyage.name: Spanish Banks
voyage.content: Is a set of three sandy beaches further west towards UBC. When the tide is out you can walk way out on the mudflats. This is a popular spot for skimboarders and kiteboarders. The area has a large stretch of beach which makes for a popular beach volleyball area as well as a scenic multi-pathway system, connecting Jericho Beach to UBC, making a fine running or cycling course. A large field behind the beach has been des

voyage.name: Wreck Beach
voyage.content: Probably North America's most famous and busiest clothing optional beach. It is a sandy beach. The trail to Wreck beach is near the West Parkade, or more precisely at the extreme west end of University Boulevard just past the Place Vanier residences. You can either park on Marine Drive or you can take transit to UBC and continue down the same road the bus brought you on foot. The steep stairs are not recommended for

voyage.name: Pacific Spirit Regional Park
voyage.content: A mostly inland park almost entirely covered with forests. It separates the University of British Columbia on the west from urban areas of Vancouver on the east. It has 55 km of hiking trails crossing through the park, of which around 30 km of trails that can be used for cycling and around 30 km can be used as equestrian trails. While It is a significantly larger park than Stanley Park, and is well used by those want

voyage.name: University Village
voyage.content: Has a number of service stores including a Staples office supply store, photocopying services, several restaurants (including a subterranean food court), a grocery, coffee shops, a liquor store, and a newsstand.

voyage.name: University Village
voyage.content: It has a full-service Starbucks Coffee as well as a Blenz, Omio Japanese Restaurant, Pita Pit, McDonald's, and a number of smaller cafes etc. An underground food court has about nine Chinese, Japanese, Indian and Persian buffets, with lunch or dinner. See listing under "Buy" for further information.

voyage.name: AMS Student Nest
voyage.content: The Nest is UBC's student union building. Within the Nest, there are a number restaurants and fast food outlets.

voyage.name: Gold Train Express
voyage.content: This rather misleadingly-named restaurant actually serves Vietnamese food, including a very good pho (beef with rice noodles).

voyage.name: Koerners Pub
voyage.content: Pub run by the Graduate Student Society. Has a patio, free pool, shuffleboard, and foosball. "Mellow Monday" open mic nights.

voyage.name: The Pit
voyage.content: A bar with a dance floor, run by the student society and famously first proposed by David Suzuki. Student ID required for Wednesday "Pit Nights" which are always packed. Inexpensive pub food served in the Burger Bar.

voyage.name: The Gallery Lounge
voyage.content: A smallish student-run pub, the Gallery is usually quieter than the Pit, and is a good place to go to grab a pint after class - and closer than Koerner's. Karaoke nights on Tuesday are a hoot, also open mic nights on Mondays and DJ nights on Fridays.

voyage.name: Pacific Spirit Hostel at UBC
voyage.content: Private or twin rooms with shared washroom and kitchen facilities. Open from mid-May to mid-August.

voyage.name: Gage Towers
voyage.content: Low-rise complex with a range of rooms. One bedroom and studio suites have private washroom and kitchenette. A tower suite room provides a private bedroom with a shared washroom and kitchenette (between 4-6 people). Open from mid-May to mid-August.

voyage.name: West Coast Suites
voyage.content: One bedroom suites with kitchenettes. Open year round.

voyage.name: HI Vancouver-Jericho Beach
voyage.price: $18-22 for a bed in the dorm
voyage.content: Open 24 hr May 1 - Sep 30. Located 100 m from the beach and between UBC campus and downtown. Beautiful and quiet park setting but the 20-25min bus ride downtown leaves some feeling isolated.

voyage.name: Queen Elizabeth Park
voyage.content: An old quarry that was converted into a number of gardens and ponds, named after Queen Elizabeth, consort of King George VI of the United Kingdom. The top of the park is the highest point in the city of Vancouver and offers views of the entire city.

voyage.name: Bloedel Conservatory
voyage.content: Tropical plants and birds under the white dome.

voyage.name: Vancouver City Hall
voyage.content: Built on the rise over False Creek, the building has nice grounds and provides a different view into downtown Vancouver and the mountains behind.

voyage.name: Vancouver Canadians
voyage.content: Vancouver's minor league (single A) baseball team.

voyage.name: Our Community Bikes
voyage.content: A community bike shop that offers space for do-it-yourself bike repairs and maintenance, as well as selling refurbished bikes.

voyage.name: Regional Assembly of Text
voyage.content: Stationery store with very pleasing pens, notebooks, and the like; delightfully whimsical booklets; and lots of fun souvenirs in the general stationery theme.

voyage.name: Hawker's Delight
voyage.content: At Main and King Edward Hawker's servers up authentic Malaysian/Singaporean dishes at $4-5. Fast-paced atmosphere (as the name would suggest). Good vegetarian options.

voyage.name: Heartwood Community Cafe
voyage.content: Successor to the popular Rhizome Cafe, serves bistro food, organic coffee, and alcoholic drinks. They seek to build community, and offer a meeting room for events.

voyage.name: Lucy's Eastside Diner
voyage.hours: 24 hours a day, 7 days a week
voyage.content: A slightly self-conscious reinvention of the classic burgers-and-pancakes diner. Being open all night long is good. Breakfast 24 hours a day is even better. The friendly and flexible service is great. The milkshakes laced with whisky, rum, and on request, bacon? Priceless. Good range of vegetarian selections. Since there aren't many all-night restaurants, Lucy's can get crowded late at night after clubs close.

voyage.name: Vera's Burger Shack
voyage.content: One of a local chain, well known for tasty, made-to-order hamburgers and a casual atmosphere. Vegetarian options and beer also served. Take-out also.

voyage.name: The Acorn
voyage.hours: Mon–Wed 5:30–10:30PM (bar open until midnight); Thu Fri 5:30–11PM (bar until 1AM); Sat 10AM–2:30PM brunch, 5:30–11PM dinner (bar until 1AM); Sun 10AM–2:30PM brunch, 5:30–10:30PM (bar open until midnight)
voyage.content: Opened in 2012, this is one of Vancouver's few restaurants to offer high cuisine that is entirely vegetarian, with many vegan and gluten-free options. Open for dinner every night and for weekend brunch. Their bar also serves creative and tasty cocktails. No reservations taken, and veggie foodies have few other options, so expect a wait unless you come soon after they open.

voyage.name: Shiro Sushi
voyage.content: If Toshi is too busy, walking west a half dozen blocks will bring you to another affordable family-run sushi restaurant with friendly service and a packet of Pocky with your bill.

voyage.name: Sun Sui Wah Seafood Restaurant
voyage.content: An excellent Chinese restaurant, the chefs are excellent cooks. Beware there are long lineups and reservations are a must.

voyage.name: Toshi Sushi
voyage.content: A small mostly family-run sushi restaurant that serves relatively cheap, good sushi. Avoid the garlic beef, but one must try the tempura. It's a popular spot so it's best to get there before 5PM.

voyage.name: Locus Restaurant
voyage.content: Local favourite with a variety of dishes that incorporate local and seasonal ingredients. Will substitute tofu for meat if requested.

voyage.name: Seasons in the Park
voyage.price: Mains run from $17 to $34. Appetizers from $7 to $13
voyage.address: 405 West 33rd Ave (at the top of Queen Elizabeth Park)
voyage.content: If the weather is nice, this restaurant has one of the best views in the city since it is the highest point in Vancouver. Surprisingly, for a restaurant with this good a location, the food and service are excellent and the prices are reasonable. Try the rack of lamb and the stuffed mushrooms. Bill Clinton and Boris Yeltsin ate here when they had their 1994 summit in Vancouver.

voyage.name: Douglas Guest House
voyage.content: Victorian house converted to B&B. Reviewers indicated the hearty breakfasts are good and the location is convenient but a couple of the rooms could be cleaner. Owned by the same owner as the Windsor House.

voyage.name: Windsor Guest House
voyage.content: Victorian house converted to B&B. Reviewers indicated the hearty breakfasts are good and the location is convenient but a couple of the rooms could be cleaner. Owned by the same owner as the Douglas House.

voyage.name: Holiday Inn - Vancouver Centre
voyage.price: $160–250 in summer, cheaper rates at other times
voyage.content: Clean rooms and courteous service, although the decor could be updated.

voyage.name: Park Inn & Suites
voyage.price: $160–300 in summer, cheaper rates at other times
voyage.content: Mix of rooms ranging from a standard hotel room to kitchenette to suites. Some rooms have views of downtown and the mountains. High-speed internet and fitness centre on site.

voyage.name: New Brighton Park
voyage.price: The park is free, $3-6 for the pool
voyage.content: Good-sized park tucked on the shore of the Burrard Inlet between port facilities. It provides an interesting, grittier view of the North Shore mountains with the port facilities and Second Narrows Bridge in sight. Amenities include playing fields, a children's playground, a beach and a trail along the shore. There is also the New Brighton Pool, a heated outdoor pool that is usually open from the Victoria Day long wee

voyage.name: Hastings Racecourse
voyage.content: Horse racing on most weekends.

voyage.name: Momiji Garden
voyage.price: Free, except when the PNE is open during the second half of August
voyage.content: Small Japanese garden built as an apology for Japanese internment.

voyage.name: East Van Cross
voyage.content: This artwork installed in 2010, looks like a Christian cross, and is a reference is to the city’s Eastern half, which is traditionally less wealthy and harder-edged. Ironically almost half of Greater Vancouver residents identify as not having a religion, a fraction that is higher than any other large city in North America. This artwork is easily seen when looking south, while taking the SkyTrain Expo Line between Mai

voyage.name: PNE
voyage.hours: Open daily from 11AM - late during the second half of August
voyage.content: Two week exhibition where extra rides and events are added to the usual Playland activities.

voyage.name: Playland at the PNE
voyage.price: $20 if under 4 feet, $30 otherwise. Parents of kids under 12 pay $13
voyage.hours: Open daily from late June through August and weekends only in May and September. Hours of operation are generally 10AM-6PM; during the PNE hours are from 11AM - late
voyage.content: Playland is a medium-sized amusement park, like something you may find at a U.S. county fair, and activities include a wooden rollercoaster, games, shows for kids and perhaps 20 or so other rides that spin, throw and hurl you in various ways.

voyage.name: East Hastings
voyage.content: Between Renfrew St and Clark Dr, especially east of Victoria Dr. Offers some of the best hidden delights in the city, including produce stores.

voyage.name: Taiga Works
voyage.content: Sells outdoors supplies.

voyage.name: Britannia Sushi
voyage.content: This might be the best deal on sushi in the city. $4.95 for an 18 piece combo (including yam rolls) with miso soup, or teriyaki box. Decent quality and decor.

voyage.name: Samurai Sushi on Fraser
voyage.content: Well known for having huge portions for small prices. Take out available. There is another location at 1108 Davie in the West End, which is open until midnight.

voyage.name: Bon's Off Broadway
voyage.content: Bon's has a great atmosphere and excellent prices including $3 breakfast all day: 2 eggs, toast, bacon or sausage, and hashbrowns.

voyage.name: La Casa Gelato
voyage.content: This gelateria is a little off the beaten path, but the over 200 flavours will reward you!

voyage.name: Ba Le
voyage.content: A Vietnamese sandwich shop that is rather out of the way for most tourists but it regularly wins local awards for sandwiches and has delicious Vietnamese subs (including a vegetarian one) for less than $8.

voyage.name: Red Wagon Cafe
voyage.content: Small neighbourhood restaurant kind of like a country diner serving hearty portions of sandwiches, burgers and all day breakfast. It's probably best known for its pulled pork pancakes and sandwiches. Popular over lunch, so expect to wait for a table if arriving between noon and 1PM.

voyage.name: Tacofino
voyage.price: $6 for a taco, $13 for a burrito
voyage.content: Taco chain that began in Tofino but now has locations all over Vancouver, the hastings branch offers a hip vibe and a large selection of craft-beer.

voyage.name: Phnom Penh
voyage.content: Authentic Cambodian restaurant which can attract large crowds.

voyage.name: Cedar Cottage Neighbourhood Pub
voyage.content: Upstairs is a funky little coffee house with lots of comfy seating, downstairs is a friendly pub, popular with a lot of local sports teams. There is a patio adjoining, with heat lamps for those cooler evenings. Friday nights are almost always packed.

voyage.name: Odd Society Spirits
voyage.content: Microdistillery with their own cocktails. They offer a tasting with a sample of each of their different liquors as well as small tours.

voyage.name: St. Augustine's Pub
voyage.content: A pub that takes its beer seriously. The two page beer menu features craft beers from across Canada and U.S. and there are live reports on how full each keg is. The food choices are pretty standard for a pub — burgers, sandwiches, pizza and finger foods — but it's well done. There are also a number of TVs for catching the game.

voyage.name: Bomber Brewing
voyage.content: Microbrewery that offers flights, snacks and sells canned 6-packs of some of their beers. Offers small tours too.

voyage.name: Parallel 49 Brewing
voyage.content: Microbrewery.

voyage.name: Powell Street Craft Brewery
voyage.hours: Mon-Thu noon-8PM, Fri-Sat noon-9PM, Sun noon-7PM
voyage.content: Microbrewery that offers flights, snacks and growler fills.

voyage.name: Storm Brewing
voyage.content: Oldest microbrewery in Vancouver. They don't offer flights, but will give you tastings of anything one at a time for free (small donation suggested).

voyage.name: Off the Rail Brewing
voyage.content: Microbrewery with a large number of beers and some snacks. They've begun offering pint cans of some of their beers and offer growler fills.

voyage.name: Atrium Inn
voyage.price: $150 and up, suites start around $240 (summer rates)
voyage.content: Standard motel room with wireless internet in each room and a complimentary continental breakfast. Located on a busy street so traffic noise can sometimes be a problem. Will provide complimentary shuttle service to downtown and some nearby attractions (although space is limited).

voyage.name: The Waldorf Hotel
voyage.content: The Waldorf is a creative hub in the heart of East Vancouver where contemporary art, music, food and culture convene under one roof. The programming for the space will be both artistically expansive and thematically inclusive. The complex consists of thirty rooms, two restaurants (Nuba Cafe and The Leeteg Dining Room), a Tiki bar (restored and retrofitted with a vintage analogue audiophile sound system), a hair salon

en.title: Visual College of Art and Design
SFU School for the Contemporary Arts
